articles.title: Barir Pujos to stick to centuries-old tradition, will have fish for bhog
articles.summary: Kolkata bonedi families reaffirm centuries-old Durga Puja rituals, including fish bhog, despite Navratri non-veg boycott calls; some ended animal sacrifice.
articles.body: KOLKATA: Bengal‘s historic bonedi families remain committed to preserving their centuries-old customs following the controversy sparked by Bageshwar Baba, who called for a boycott of people who consume non-vegetarian food during Navrarti. Rather than engaging in external debates, these households, including Sabarna Roy Chowdhury’s descendants and one wing of Sovabazar Rajbari, view their long-standing rituals — such as offering non-vegetarian bhog — as an inherent expression of their ancestral heritage and family faith.For these custodian families, continuing these practices is simply a matter of honuoring their legacy-driven traditions that have defined their family worship for hundreds of years. Tanmoy Roy Chowdhury, secretary of the management committee for the Borobari Durga Puja of the Sabarna Roy Chowdhury family, said the tradition of offering non-vegetarian bhog spans 300 years. “A part of our family also offers the Atchala puja which is 400 years old. In both pujas, katla fish is offered for bhog on Nabami,” he noted. “We catch the fish from a pond behind our house, which is then cooked and served as bhog. If a family member desires, any other kind of fish can also be offered as bhog.” Addressing non-veg commentary, he added, "I have nothing to say about Baba's advice or whatever else anyone is saying. We will continue following the rituals that have been part of our family heritage for centuries." He also referenced the family's past practices, sharing that "that inhuman practice" of animal sacrifice was discontinued around 30 to 35 years ago.If ‘katla’ is a favourite with the Roy Chowdhury descendants, catfish finds pride of place at the Sovabazar Rajbari (“Boro Torof”). Soumit Narayan Deb, ninth generation of Maharaja Nabakrishna Deb Bahadur of Sovabazar Rajbari (“Boro Torof”), rewinds to 1858 when Raja Sir Radhakanta Deb Bahadur stopped goat sacrifice and offered his own blood instead. “Since blood is necessary for the worship of Shakti, all important pundits were summoned from all over India to thakurdalan of the Sovabazar Rajbari. They discussed alternative options if the descendants refused to offer their own blood and finally decided that catfish would be offered as sacrifice.”Since then, catfish is sacrificed at the alter of this ‘bonedi’ house. “The fish is offered to the goddess. The body is taken to the thakurdalan while its head is taken home by the one who sacrifices the catfish at the altar. The goddess is also offered rohu fish and vegetables. This is described as ‘siddha‘. The purohit then takes the ‘siddha’ home after the Nabami puja is over. Our Puja started in 1757 and this tradition has been going on since there. Who says what doesn’t affect our tradition,” Deb said.Marking its 167th year, the Chorbagan Chatterjee family Durga Puja continues its traditional daily ritual of offering fish bhogs —including hilsa, bhekti, and pona — from Saptami to Dashami. Family member Hijal Chatterjee said, “We will not make any changes to this as it is our family tradition. The concept behind this is that Durga is considered our daughter who visits with her family. So, we offer the best items on the menu.”While Janbazar Rani Rashmoni’s family offers a vegetarian bhog to the deity, they continue the tradition of serving non-vegetarian items to guests on Saptami and Nabami. Prasun Hazra, a sixth-generation descendant from Mathuramohan’s lineage, said, “Our puja is approximately 234 years old. Prior to 2003, we used to have ‘Pathabali‘ (goat sacrifice), but we stopped that ritual in 2003. Now, we offer a strictly vegetarian bhog to the Goddess, but we serve non-vegetarian items to our guests on Saptami and Nabami. We respect everyone’s food choices—even though my wife and I follow a strict vegetarian diet during the four days of Puja to perform the rituals, we never impose this practice on our guests.”You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Kolkata | Silver Rate in Kolkata | Bank Holidays in Kolkata | Public Holidays in Kolkata | Kolkata AQI | Weather in Kolkata | Petrol Price in Kolkata | Diesel Price in Kolkata | CNG Price in Kolkata | LPG Price in KolkataStay updated with the latest Kolkata news. articles.title: Professora agredida por aluno em SP diz que indenização é irrisória | G1
articles.standfirst: Profissional ficou cerca de oito meses afastada após ser empurrada por adolescente em Cubatão. Justiça manteve condenação do Governo de SP por danos morais.
articles.summary: Após ser empurrada por aluno em Cubatão, professora contesta indenização de R$ 5 mil e relata prejuízos físicos e psicológicos causados pela agressão.
articles.body:
Professora agredida terá que retornar à escola em Cubatão (SP) com hematomas — Foto: Matheus Croce/TV Tribuna e arquivo pessoal

A professora Edna Maria Ribeiro, de 64 anos, que foi agredida por um aluno em uma escola pública de Cubatão (SP) , em 2024, considerou "irrisória" a indenização de R$ 5 mil por danos morais fixada pela Justiça contra o Governo do Estado. Para ela, o valor não corresponde aos impactos físicos, psicológicos e financeiros provocados pela agressão.

A agressão ocorreu depois que a professora, à época com 62 anos, retirou o adolescente de 15 anos da sala de aula porque ele conversava durante uma prova. Edna foi empurrada, caiu sobre uma lixeira metálica e sofreu hematomas no rosto e no tronco.

Segundo a professora, as lesões fizeram com que ela ficasse afastada do trabalho por cerca de oito meses, período em que recebeu o Auxílio por Incapacidade Temporária do Instituto Nacional do Seguro Social (INSS).

Edna afirmou que o benefício tinha valor inferior ao salário que recebia como professora e que, durante o afastamento, acumulou dívidas com aluguel e contas básicas, posteriormente pagas com juros.

Mesmo após retornar ao trabalho, em agosto de 2025, ela disse que ainda enfrenta reflexos financeiros do período. A professora também afirmou que passou a sentir mais ansiedade dentro da sala de aula após a agressão.

Edna disse ainda que nem mesmo os cerca de R$ 56 mil pedidos inicialmente no processo seriam suficientes para reparar os danos.

“Não é justo o professor estar em sala de aula, para ensinar várias coisas que são importantes até para a própria vida do aluno, e ele ainda ser agredido tanto verbalmente quanto fisicamente”, afirmou.

Apesar da insatisfação com o valor fixado, Edna acredita que a indenização ainda pode ser elevada pela Justiça. Segundo ela, os advogados devem apresentar um pedido no processo.

Professora ficou com a região dos olhos com hematomas após virar para não bater o nariz — Foto: Matheus Croce/TV Tribuna

A professora acionou a Justiça em novembro de 2024 e pediu cerca de R$ 56 mil em indenizações. Ela alegou ter sofrido danos físicos e psicológicos e afirmou que o Estado foi omisso no dever de garantir a segurança no ambiente escolar.

Segundo Edna, o aluno já tinha histórico de comportamento agressivo antes do episódio.

Em abril deste ano, a Justiça acolheu o pedido de indenização, mas fixou o valor dos danos morais em R$ 5 mil.

O Governo do Estado recorreu ao Tribunal de Justiça de São Paulo (TJ-SP) e alegou que a agressão ocorreu exclusivamente por causa da conduta do aluno. Segundo a Procuradoria, a ação do adolescente "sequer poderia ser prevista pela direção da escola".

O Estado também afirmou que a agressão "extrapola o poder de vigilância dos funcionários do estabelecimento de ensino" e alegou que não havia relação entre eventual omissão estatal e o dano moral sofrido pela professora.

Professora agredida terá que retornar à escola em Cubatão (SP) com hematomas — Foto: Matheus Croce/TV Tribuna

A 2ª Turma Recursal da Fazenda Pública do TJ-SP, porém, manteve a decisão.

A relatora do recurso, juíza Lúcia Caninéo Campanhã, afirmou que o Estado tinha a obrigação de zelar pelo bem-estar dos funcionários durante a jornada de trabalho.

A magistrada também considerou que, devido ao histórico do aluno, o episódio não poderia ser considerado totalmente inesperado.

"Assim, não se trata sequer de agressão inesperada, posto que ocorreu após desentendimento, e o aluno agressor já tinha histórico de desentendimento", afirmou.

Os juízes Wander Pereira Rossette Júnior e Érico Di Prospero Gentil Leite acompanharam o voto da relatora. O colegiado também determinou que o Estado arque com os honorários advocatícios, fixados em 15% sobre o valor da condenação.

articles.title: Unicamp tem tratativas para criação do curso de medicina em Piracicaba | G1
articles.standfirst: Iniciativa envolve debate sobre plano da prefeitura que prevê implantação de distrito de inovação na cidade. Projeto deve ser enviado à Câmara em outubro.
articles.summary: Iniciativa envolve debate sobre plano da prefeitura que prevê implantação de distrito de inovação na cidade.
articles.body:
A Faculdade de Odontologia de Piracicaba (FOP) da Unicamp — Foto: Yasmin Moscoski/g1

A Unicamp confirmou, em nota enviada ao g1 na última semana, que conversas estão em andamento para viabilizar a criação do curso de medicina em Piracicaba (SP).

O assunto veio à tona na quarta-feira (9), durante uma reunião da prefeitura com representantes do Governo de São Paulo, USP e da própria Unicamp para tratar sobre a criação do Distrito de Inovação de Piracicaba.

🔎 Distritos de inovação são territórios urbanos em que universidades, centros de pesquisa, empresas e poder público se concentram e se conectam para gerar conhecimento, negócios e qualidade de vida.

À reportagem, a diretora do campus da Unicamp em Piracicaba, professora Karina Gonzales Silvério, ressaltou que a criação do curso de medicina em Piracicaba, assim como a de outros cursos de graduação, depende da concretização de um projeto de autarquização da área de saúde da universidade.

🔎 Uma autarquia de saúde é uma entidade pública com autonomia administrativa e financeira, criada por lei específica para executar serviços e gerenciar políticas públicas de saúde de forma descentralizada.

"Com o andamento desse projeto de autarquização, libera recursos dentro da Unicamp que possibilitará ampliar o oferecimento dos cursos de graduação, incluindo a medicina aqui em Piracicaba", destacou.

Por conta disso, ainda não há um prazo para que esses novos cursos sejam criados nem o total de vagas que eles oferecerão.

O g1 também pediu mais detalhes do projeto à Prefeitura de Piracicaba, que informou que apenas a Unicamp poderia se manifestar sobre o assunto.

A reunião de quarta-feira serviu para definir como será o andamento do projeto para a implantação do Distrito de Inovação em Piracicaba.

Uma lei estadual estabelece requisitos para que um distrito de inovação seja reconhecido pelo Estado, entre eles estão: a existência de organizações âncoras, área definida, plano de implantação e prestação de contas anual.

“Com a participação da USP e da Unicamp ao lado do Estado e do município, Piracicaba passa a contar com quatro instituições âncoras, quando o mínimo exigido pela política estadual é de duas”, diz a prefeitura.

Diante disso, a administração municipal cita que os próximos passos do projeto são a definição da governança do distrito e a elaboração do plano de implantação, ambos também previstos na política estadual.

Simultaneamente, a prefeitura pretende finalizar o Sistema Municipal de Desenvolvimento Sustentável (Simdes), que é um projeto de lei que reúne incentivos e dá base legal ao distrito. A previsão é de que esse projeto seja protocolado na Câmara Municipal em outubro deste ano.

articles.title: Pesquisa transforma rama de mandioca descartada em alimento para gado | G1
articles.standfirst: Descoberta é uma alternativa nutritiva e de baixo custo para reduzir os impactos da escassez de pasto durante o período de seca, um dos principais desafios enfrentados pelos pecuaristas.
articles.summary: Descoberta é uma alternativa nutritiva e de baixo custo para reduzir os impactos da escassez de pasto durante o período de seca, um dos principais desafios enfrentados pelos pecuar
articles.body:
O que antes era descartado nas lavouras de mandioca pode se tornar uma alternativa para alimentar rebanhos durante a seca em Mato Grosso. Em parceria com a Empresa Mato-grossense de Pesquisa, Assistência e Extensão Rural (Empaer) , pesquisadores d a Universidade Federal de Mato Grosso (UFMT) desenvolvem um estudo que utiliza a parte aérea da mandioca — o terço superior da planta geralmente descartado — como suplemento nutritivo, sustentável e de baixo custo para a alimentação dos animais , especialmente durante o período de estiagem no estado.

🔍 O calor intenso em Mato Grosso ocorre principalmente por causa do período de estiagem. Nesta época, a quantidade de chuva diminui, o ar fica mais seco e há menos nuvens para bloquear a radiação solar. Com isso, o solo e o ambiente aquecem mais durante o dia, elevando as temperaturas e mantendo o tempo quente por vários dias.

O estudo é desenvolvido pelo Grupo de Estudos e Extensão em Forragicultura e Conservação de Forragens (GEFOR) , vinculado à Faculdade de Agronomia e Zootecnia da UFMT, sob orientação do professor Dr. Joadil Gonçalves de Abreu . Segundo ele, a proposta é oferecer uma alternativa nutritiva e de baixo custo para reduzir os impactos da escassez de pasto durante a seca, um dos principais desafios enfrentados pelos pecuaristas da região.

A Empaer desenvolve pesquisas com mandioca desde 2012, buscando identificar cultivares mais adaptadas às diferentes regiões de Mato Grosso e aumentar a produtividade. Além da pesquisa, a instituição trabalha para levar os resultados aos agricultores por meio de galhos do topo da mandioca, dias de campo, reuniões técnicas e orientações aos produtores .

Na UFMT , a pesquisa ainda está em fase inicial . Até o momento, foram analisadas algumas variedades de mandioca destinadas à indústria. Ainda falta avaliar as variedades de mandioca de mesa. Após a conclusão das análises, os resultados poderão ser publicados e apresentados aos produtores, inclusive durante os dias de campo promovidos pela universidade.

Mandioca de mesa é aquela produzida principalmente para o consumo humano, como a mandioca cozida ou usada em receitas.

Mandioca industrial é cultivada principalmente para a produção de farinha, fécula, amido e outros derivados.

Tradicionalmente, a mandioca é cultivada visando a comercialização de suas raízes e o aproveitamento do caule grosso para novos plantios. As folhas e ramos do topo, no entanto, costumam ser deixados no campo. A pesquisa do GEFOR, realizada em parceria com a Empaer — através da pesquisadora e engenheira agrônoma Dra. Dolorice Moreti —, identificou que esse material descartado é um verdadeiro " superalimento " para o gado.

Em pleno período de estiagem, as pastagens convencionais sofrem uma queda drástica de qualidade, registrando cerca de 5% a 6% de proteína bruta. Para não perder peso, um boi precisa de, no mínimo, 7%.

"A parte aérea da mandioca, em nossos dados, superou os 15% de proteína bruta, chegando a mais de 20% em algumas cultivares específicas, é um alimento que, além de manter o animal, garante ganho de peso em plena seca" destacou o professor Joadil.

Além da alta qualidade, a produtividade impressiona. Em testes de campo, a cultura atingiu a marca de 28 toneladas de massa verde por hectare . Para efeito de comparação, híbridos de milho utilizados para silagem produzem cerca de 35 toneladas. A proximidade dos números surpreende os pesquisadores, visto que a mandioca sequer é uma cultura melhorada geneticamente para a produção de folhas, e sim de raízes.

"Quando comparamos a produção de massa verde, percebemos que a mandioca se aproxima da produtividade do milho para silagem, mas com uma grande vantagem: ela suporta muito melhor os períodos de estiagem", destaca Joadil.

O trabalho na Empaer consiste em validar o comportamento desses materiais genéticos (provenientes da Embrapa, IAC e outros órgãos) nas diferentes regiões do estado. No Campo Experimental de Tangará da Serra, a instituição mantém hoje um banco vivo impressionante:

70 materiais genéticos de mandioca de mesa (de polpa branca, amarela e rosada);

25 materiais genéticos de mandioca voltados para a indústria.

Além do desenvolvimento de cultivares mais produtivas, as pesquisas também acompanham a evolução das tecnologias adotadas pelos agricultores. Segundo a pesquisadora, nos últimos anos os produtores passaram a investir cada vez mais em análise de solo, correção da fertilidade, adubação e irrigação, práticas que potencializam o desempenho das variedades melhoradas.

"Não avaliamos apenas produtividade. Observamos resistência a doenças, qualidade culinária, teor de amido, arquitetura da planta e adaptação às diferentes regiões do estado. O objetivo é recomendar ao produtor materiais que realmente tragam retorno econômico", afirmou Dolorice.

Antes de ser oferecida aos animais, a parte da mandioca que fica acima do solo precisa passar por um período de secagem. Segundo o professor Joadil, esse processo reduz a presença de uma substância natural da planta que pode liberar compostos tóxicos e causar problemas de saúde nos animais quando o material ainda está úmido.

"O único cuidado que a gente sempre ressalta é fazer a secagem. O produtor não pode picar e fornecer o material úmido para o animal, porque existe o risco de morte por asfixia devido à presença do ácido cianídrico. Depois que o material seca, esse composto volatiliza e o alimento pode ser utilizado com segurança", explica o professor.

A solução encontrada pelo grupo é simples, barata e eficiente: a produção de feno .

Picagem : O material é triturado em pedaços de aproximadamente 2 centímetros.

Secagem : O conteúdo é estendido sobre lonas plásticas ao sol e revirado a cada hora. Como o ácido cianídrico é volátil, ele evapora completamente durante o processo.

Teste do Sal : Para saber se está no ponto, os estudantes misturam o material com sal de cozinha; se o sal não grudar na planta, o feno está pronto e totalmente seguro para o consumo.

A proporção média é de que uma tonelada de massa verde resulte em 200 a 300 kg de feno . Essa quantidade é suficiente para alimentar até 25 animais adultos por um dia , considerando o consumo médio de 10 kg diários por cabeça.

Além de servir para consumo próprio, o feno ensacado surge como uma nova fonte de renda para agricultores que não possuem rebanho, permitindo a comercialização do subproduto para criadores de bovinos, caprinos e ovinos da região.

Etapa de secagem da mandioca antes do uso na alimentação animal. — Foto: Giovanna Baiocco/ g1 MT

Para além dos laboratórios, o projeto cumpre um papel social e pedagógico fundamental. Os estudantes e bolsistas de iniciação tecnológica (PIBITI), João Henrique (7º período de Agronomia) e Camila Neves (9º período de Zootecnia), enfrentam a rotina pesada do campo na fazenda experimental da UFMT para fazer a pesquisa acontecer.

"Na seca é muito complicado. Teve momentos em que precisamos ir no final de semana para conseguir irrigar o campo experimental por conta da rotina cheia de aulas" [...] "Muitos produtores jogam isso fora por falta de informação. Passar esse conhecimento e ver que a prática resolve gargalos que a teoria sozinha não mostra é gratificante," relata João Henrique.

Camila reforçou também o impacto econômico da alternativa sustentável.

"Muitos querem usar apenas o milho, que é caro. A mandioca é rústica, barata e exige pouca adubação. Essa vivência abre nossa cabeça para ajudar o pequeno produtor a crescer," acrescenta Camila.

Mesmo com os resultados promissores, Dolorice disse que o trabalho está apenas começando e que a pesquisa precisa ser permanente para acompanhar as demandas do setor.

"A pesquisa precisa ser contínua e dinâmica, porque sempre surgem novos problemas e novas tecnologias que precisam ser avaliadas. Hoje em Tangará, temos cerca de 70 materiais genéticos de mandioca de mesa e outros 25 destinados à indústria. Muitos já foram avaliados e outros ainda estão em fase de multiplicação. Precisamos garantir condições para continuar esse trabalho", ressaltou.

Da mandioca descartada, uma nova alternativa para o gado. 🌱🐂 — Foto: g1 MT

A parceria entre UFMT e Empaer planeja realizar, no início do próximo ano agrícola, um Dia de Campo voltado aos produtores rurais de Santo Antônio de Leverger e região. Durante o evento, os alunos envolvidos na pesquisa, juntamente com o professor Joadil, irão apresentar as técnicas de aproveitamento da parte aérea da mandioca, a produção do feno e as novas cultivares avaliadas. A atividade também irá apresentar formas de utilização da planta e os resultados obtidos no estudo.

articles.title: ‘Western troops in Ukraine would mean war with Russia’: Putin ahead of Brics meet
articles.summary: Europe News: Russian President Vladimir Putin on Saturday warned that discussions about deploying foreign troops to Ukraine would effectively amount to a declarati.
articles.body: Russian President Vladimir Putin on Saturday warned that discussions about deploying foreign troops to Ukraine would effectively amount to a declaration of war against Russia.Speaking on the sidelines of the Brics Summit, Putin remarked, "Now they are talking about how they are thinking about bringing troops to the territory of Ukraine. This means war with Russia."Addressing suggestions that Russia poses a threat to European nations amid the ongoing war in Ukraine, the Russian leader firmly rejected the notion."There is no such threat, and there has never been. We are not threatening European countries, nor are we going to threaten them. Why would we?" Putin said.He argued that there was no basis for any dispute between Russia and Europe, stating that all outstanding matters had been resolved following the second world war.Putin's remarks arrive as the war with Ukraine continues in its fifth year. Since then, several European countries have continued to back Ukraine, while the United States has sought to play the role of mediator, facilitating talks between Moscow and Kyiv.Turning to political developments within Europe, Putin also commented on the recent rise of Germany's far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) party, which topped the state election in Saxony-Anhalt earlier this month.He described the current state of affairs across Europe as the outcome of "systemic mistakes" made by the West in the fields of politics, security and economics."Everyone makes mistakes. We have made quite a few mistakes ourselves, as has the rest of the world," Putin acknowledged, before adding that the West's "globalists" had, since the end of the Cold War and the fall of the Soviet Union, come to see themselves as being at the "top of Olympus", believing both that they could act without constraint and that they were incapable of error.According to exit poll figures released by German broadcaster ARD and reported by Al Jazeera, the AfD won 44.5 per cent of the vote in Saxony-Anhalt, more than double the 18.5 per cent secured by Chancellor Friedrich Merz's centre-right Christian Democratic Union (CDU).This marks the first time since the Second World War that a far-right party has come first in a German state election.The AfD has never been part of a governing coalition at either state or federal level, with mainstream parties upholding a long-standing refusal to work with it, a barrier widely known as the "firewall".Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: In 2008,  Larry Page demolished two neighbouring Palo Alto homes, expanding his compound to nearly 2 acres; a year later he planned a 6,000-sq-ft eco-house with solar panels and a roof garden
articles.summary: US News: Google co-founder Larry Page’s Palo Alto property plans drew attention in the late 2000s as he began acquiring neighbouring homes and expanding the la.
articles.body: Google co-founder Larry Page’s Palo Alto property plans drew attention in the late 2000s as he began acquiring neighbouring homes and expanding the land around his residence. In 2008, two houses on Bryant Street were demolished after Page acquired the properties, adding them to his existing holdings and creating a compound of nearly two acres. A year later, plans emerged for a nearly 6,000-square-foot environmentally friendly house on an adjacent lot. According to the Mountain View Voice, the proposed home was designed with solar panels, a roof garden and several features intended to reduce its environmental impact.Page began assembling neighbouring propertiesPage’s expansion in Palo Alto was not simply about building a larger house. He was gradually acquiring properties around his existing residence in the Old Palo Alto neighbourhood, a part of the city known for its mature trees, large homes and high property values. According to the Palo Alto Daily Post, Page had purchased and demolished the former homes at 2131 and 2161 Bryant Street in 2008. One of the properties had belonged to Palo Alto businessman and philanthropist Len Ely, whose historic home had been placed on the market after being left to Stanford University.Page had also acquired a roughly half-acre property at 330 Santa Rita Avenue. Following a property swap with another wealthy neighbour, Page gained an additional 1.18 acres fronting Bryant Street. Combined with the Hacienda de Lemos property where he reportedly lived, the acquisitions brought his holdings on the block to nearly two acres. The scale of the acquisitions attracted attention because several older houses were being removed from a neighbourhood where large, established homes were already part of the landscape. The Palo Alto Daily Post described the area as increasingly resembling a “billionaires' alley,” while residents expressed concern about how new construction could change the character of Old Palo Alto.A nearly 6,000-square-foot house was plannedBy March 2009, Page was preparing plans for another substantial house on a more than 0.75-acre lot. The Mountain View Voice reported that the proposed residence would measure nearly 6,000 square feet and stand two storeys tall, with four bedrooms and a full basement. The planned house was also notable because Page was not simply pursuing size. His spokesman said the design was intended to minimise the home's environmental impact. More than 60 existing trees were expected to remain on the property, helping screen the building from the street and neighbouring homes.The plans came at a time when Palo Alto's rules placed limits on residential development. According to the Mountain View Voice, Page could have built close to 11,000 square feet on the lot, but the proposed residence was kept to about 6,000 square feet.Solar panels and a roof gardenThe environmental features were central to the proposed design. Page was seeking GreenPoint certification, a programme that recognised homes incorporating environmentally preferable construction and design measures. The planned house was to include a roof garden with solar panels. It would also use recycled materials and materials with low or no volatile organic compound emissions. The design included grasscrete pavers, pervious paving in the parking court and a permeable pathway through the trees, allowing rainwater to seep into the ground rather than simply running off paved surfaces.Page was also working with an arborist to address the condition of trees on the property. Some unhealthy trees were expected to be replaced with varieties requiring less water, an especially relevant consideration in California's dry climate.A luxury project shaped around environmental designThe proposed residence combined the scale expected of a Silicon Valley billionaire's property with an unusually strong emphasis on environmental features for its time. The exterior was planned with zinc cladding and extensive glazing, including a large wall of sliding-glass doors at the rear. The project also reflected the broader transformation taking place around Page's Palo Alto properties. articles.title: At 21, an Australian artist bought 25 acres in Tasmania; 18 months later a bushfire destroyed her first home, so she rebuilt it from salvage materials into an off-grid cabin for AU$7,000-10,000
articles.summary: Rest of World News: An Australian artist who used her savings to buy a 25-acre bush block in Tasmania at the age of 21 has built an off-grid home using salvaged materials.
articles.body: An Australian artist who used her savings to buy a 25-acre bush block in Tasmania at the age of 21 has built an off-grid home using salvaged materials after a bushfire destroyed her original house just 18 months after she moved in. After losing her first home and having limited money left, she decided not to use a traditional homebuilder. Instead, she spent months collecting discarded timber, metal sheets and old building materials from salvage yards and fire-damaged sites across the island. She used them to build a self-contained cabin for an estimated AU$7,000 to AU$10,000. According to a feature published by alternative housing publication Tiny House Talk, the project shows how using salvaged materials can provide a low-cost way to build a home, especially for young Australians facing high housing costs and increasing environmental risks. The rebuilt home is completely off the electricity and water grids. It uses rooftop solar panels, battery storage and rainwater tanks to meet the owner's basic needs in the remote Tasmanian countryside.Bushfire destruction led to a low-cost rebuildThe artist originally bought the land to create a studio and get away from rising rents in cities. Just 18 months after moving in, a bushfire swept through the area, destroying her first home and much of the surrounding vegetation. Instead of leaving the property or taking on a large mortgage, she decided to rebuild using cheaper and recycled materials, a method highlighted by independent housing publications such as Tiny House Talk. She collected structural timber, corrugated iron sheets and secondhand glass windows to build a small, single-storey cabin. Friends and local tradespeople also helped with heavy work and some specialist electrical connections. The design focuses on keeping the cabin warm and making it better able to withstand fire. Metal sheets on the outside provide a non-combustible layer, while the windows were positioned to make better use of sunlight for heating during Tasmania's cold winters. Inside, reclaimed wooden floorboards and reused timber panels were used for much of the interior. This helped reduce building costs while giving old materials another use instead of sending them to landfill.Off-grid systems keep living costs lowThe cabin uses its own power and water systems instead of relying on public utilities. These systems were designed to work with Tasmania's changing weather conditions. Electricity comes from a small solar panel system connected to a deep-cycle battery bank. It provides enough power for LED lights, refrigeration and charging electronic devices. Cooking is done using bottled gas and a traditional cast-iron wood-burning stove, which also provides the main source of heat during winter. Water comes from rainwater collected from the cabin's metal roof. The water flows into storage tanks, passes through filters and is then fed into the kitchen and bathroom through gravity. A dry composting toilet removes the need for a septic tank or connection to a public sewer system. This cuts both installation costs and future maintenance expenses. By keeping the initial building cost below AU$10,000 and avoiding regular utility bills, the owner has kept her monthly costs low. This has allowed her to focus on her art without the financial pressure of a traditional mortgage.Tasmania cabin reflects wider interest in alternative homesThe project is part of a wider interest in alternative housing in Australia, where high property prices and interest rates have encouraged some people to consider smaller homes, recycled materials and off-grid technology. Building industry reports show growing interest in options such as tiny houses on wheels, converted shipping containers and self-built timber cabins, particularly in rural areas where land can be cheaper than in major cities. However, alternative housing projects can face planning and safety challenges. Local council rules and strict fire regulations can make it difficult to obtain approval for homes built with unusual designs or salvaged materials, especially in areas at high risk of bushfires. The completed Tasmanian cabin shows how careful design and the use of reclaimed materials can help property owners rebuild after extreme weather without taking on large amounts of debt. The owner continues to look after her 25-acre bush block, allowing native vegetation to grow back around the cabin while living full-time in the home she built herself.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: In 2021, Malaysian police steamrolled 1,069 Bitcoin-mining machines worth about $1.25 million; the machines were allegedly linked to stolen electricity
articles.summary: Rest of World News: In a bid to tackle electricity theft linked to illegal Bitcoin mining, Malaysian police destroyed 1,069 mining machines worth $1.25 million, sending a stern warning against power theft and its consequences.
articles.body: In July 2021, 1,069 confiscated bitcoin mining units, worth a total of 5.3 million ringgit ($1.25 million), were lined up in the parking lot of a police station in Miri and crushed one by one with steamrollers, the culmination of several joint raids that police in Miri, Sarawak, and Sarawak Energy Berhad had carried out between February and April 2021, according to Bernama and The Star. Police said evidence gathered from miners who had illegally tapped SEB's power lines showed losses of 8.4 million ringgit (about $2 million). As a result, eight people were detained, and six of them were charged with electricity theft under Section 379 of Malaysia's Penal Code, drawing sentences of up to eight months in jail and fines of up to 8,000 ringgit (about $1,900), The Star reported. The Electricity Supply Act 1990 allows for stiffer penalties under Section 37(1), which some reports put at up to 1 million ringgit in fines and 10 years in prison for tampering with installations in a way that endangers life or property, while other accounts and the government's own published version of the Act cite a lower ceiling of 100,000 ringgit and five years. Across Malaysia and in several other countries, cheap or free electricity can make illegal mining more attractive for people looking to cash in on crypto without paying for the power it takes to run.The raid destroyed machines worth roughly $1.25 millionThe 1,069 rigs were seized in six raids carried out between February and April 2021 in Borneo, in a joint operation by the Miri police and SEB, the state utility company, which valued the equipment at 5.3 million ringgit, or roughly $1.25 million at the exchange rate at the time, and put its own loss from the theft at 8.4 million ringgit. Rather than letting the hardware return to use, as happened in China earlier that year, Malaysia decided to destroy it. Assistant Commissioner Hakemal Hawari, the leading police officer handling the case in Miri, stated that this was done following an intelligence report regarding miners connecting to SEB's power grid.Electricity theft was valued at close to $2 millionThe SEB estimated that they had been robbed of 8.4 million ringgit, which is about $2 million based on 2021 exchange rates. A total of eight people were arrested in relation to the theft of electricity to mine bitcoins, and six of them faced charges in court under Section 379 of Malaysia's Penal Code, with fines of up to 8,000 ringgit (about $1,900). Hawari further associated the electricity theft with three house fires in the area, and also stated that overloaded, unauthorised wiring could cause power outages and endanger lives. Section 37(1) of the Electricity Supply Act 1990 is also cited by some reports as carrying penalties of up to 1 million ringgit in fines and 10 years' imprisonment for tampering with installations in a way that endangers life or property, though other reports and the government's own published version of the Act put the maximum at 100,000 ringgit and five years.Why mining machines draw so much power in the first placeBitcoin mining is an energy-intensive process, requiring nonstop calculations to verify transactions and generate new coins, and the more computing power the network throws at the problem, the harder those calculations become. In an August 2023 report titled "Bitcoin electricity consumption: an improved assessment," Alexander Neumueller, research lead at the Cambridge Centre for Alternative Finance, revised the group's 2022 estimate of the network's annual electricity use down from 105.3 terawatt hours to 95.5 terawatt hours, after finding that outdated assumptions about the efficiency of ASIC mining hardware had overstated demand.A 2022 paper in the journal Energy & Environment, by researchers Dindar and Gül, looked specifically at how utilities can identify mining farms that are stealing power. As mentioned by the authors, the primary evidence lies in the electricity signature and not in the usage of power. In their experiments conducted on the neutral line of the power grid, they found specific harmonics generated by mining data centers, which indicate that the power companies may identify illicit farms through monitoring the quality of electricity data.Malaysia's crackdown fits a wider regional patternMalay Mail reported in March 2021 that Melaka police were hunting a bitcoin miner accused of causing about 9 million ringgit ($2.2 million) in losses to the utility company Tenaga Nasional Berhad (TNB). Three months later, China's province of Sichuan took measures to shut down its mining activities due to environmental reasons, leading the miners to move to less restrictive locations. In Malaysia, destroying the devices rather than reselling them appears intended as a warning to would-be miners elsewhere: Miri's police chief said that, for now, there are no other active mining operations left in the area. Together, the Cambridge and Energy & Environment research point to the same underlying vulnerability: wherever electricity is cheap to steal and oversight is thin, mining's power costs make theft profitable enough to keep tempting operators. While the steamroller in Miri made for a striking image, the more effective fix, the detection research suggests, is stopping the theft right at the meter.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: In 2025, crews lifted a 3,100-tonne mining machine 2.5 metres off the ground and placed it on 140 SPMT axles; it traveled 27 km in 10 days
articles.summary: Rest of World News: In August 2025, Mammoet set a new record by relocating a 6.8-million-pound dragline machine across BHP Mitsubishi Alliance's Peak Downs coal mine in Queensland. This 27 km journey, completed in just 10 days, showcases innovative engineering solutions in heavy transport logistics.
articles.body: A dragline was never meant to be moved the way it was in August 2025. The machine was a 3,100-tonne Marion 8050 dragline operating at BHP Mitsubishi Alliance's (BMA) Peak Downs coal mine in central Queensland, according to Mammoet's own case study and trade coverage from Project Cargo Journal and World Coal. Normally, a dragline relocates by "walking": shoes or pontoons alternately lift and shuffle it forward. Mammoet's own case study says a dragline moving this way covers only about 1 km every 12 hours and typically takes more than a month to cover a distance like this 27 km route. In August 2025, Mammoet relocated the dragline the full 27 km across the lease in just 10 days, which the company and trade press, including Mining Magazine, described as a new benchmark for dragline transport. Mammoet's own case study puts the average at about 8 km a day, though 27 km divided over 10 days works out closer to 2.7 km a day. The higher figure likely reflects only the days the convoy was actively moving, since the 10-day window also covered jacking the dragline up, building the rail crossing, and jacking it back down, none of which involved forward travel.The machine had to cross a live export rail lineThe mine sits in Queensland's Bowen Basin, where BHP Mitsubishi Alliance (BMA) runs several large open-cut coal mines, including Peak Downs, as BHP's own site describes the region. HLPFI reported that the dragline was needed for coal extraction in the southern pits. Between the two sites runs an Aurizon rail line that Mammoet branch manager Laura Ewen described as "a critical line, transporting coal from different mines in the region to the coast for exporting." A conventional dragline move over that distance would have kept the crossing shut for weeks, so rather than letting the machine walk, BMA brought in heavy-transport specialist Mammoet.Jacking towers lifted 6.8 million pounds clear of the groundRather than letting the Marion 8050 walk, Mammoet's crew used eight JS500 jacking towers to raise the 3,100-tonne machine about 2.5 metres off the mine floor, according to World Coal, HLPFI, and Crane & Transport Briefing. Traditional dragline jacking in Australia instead used climbing jacks with timber stacked manually underneath the load, added to as it rose, Mammoet project manager Jack Whittaker said. After jacking, the dragline was lowered onto five groups of SPMTs with 28 axles each, 140 axles in total, HLPFI reported.Ten days, eight kilometres a day and one fixed deadlineMammoet said the convoy covered the 27 km in 10 days at an average of about 8 km a day (a figure that, as noted above, likely reflects active-travel days rather than the full 10-day window), well below the SPMTs' top speed of 5 km an hour. The gap reflects how much of each day went to scheduling around inspections, heat, and the rail crossing rather than to driving. Mining Magazine and other trade outlets covering the project described the pace as record-breaking for dragline transport in Australia.Mammoet and BMA had only a 72-hour window to build a temporary ramp and tow the dragline across the Aurizon line; missing it would have delayed the project by three months, since the next rail closure wouldn't come around again that soon, Mammoet branch manager Laura Ewen said. Distributing a load this heavy across rubber rather than steel tracks or hydraulic feet is a well-studied engineering problem in its own right. In the year 2020, the paper “Optimization Solutions for Self-Propelled Modular Transporter (SPMT) Load-Outs Based on Ballast Simulation” by Haiming Zhu, Zunfeng Du, Dong Xu and Yougang Tang discusses the distribution of weight in an SPMT such that none of the suspension groups carry weight above the capability ofGround bearing capacity is the limiting factor, not horsepowerThe same reasoning is central to the Manual on the Use of Self-propelled Modular Transporters for Removal and Replacement of Bridges that was prepared by the United States' Federal Highway Administration, along with its state and industry collaborators. The section on ground-bearing capacity in its design chapter elaborates on how engineers determine the maximum force that the soil/pavement can withstand without the risk of a transporter sinking or moving. This factor is more important than engine horsepower when routing. That is what Mammoet had to contend with at Peak Downs: The machine being old, there were no records on how it distributed weight, which meant that its center of gravity had to be estimated using other similar machines.A record built on logistics, not raw sizeMammoet previously used the same jack-and-carry method in Queensland in 2017, relocating another dragline for BMA over a shorter distance, according to the company's case study. What made the 2025 relocation notable, in Mammoet's own account and in trade coverage that called it record-breaking, was less the distance than the constraints: a 3,100-tonne machine on a fixed schedule with a live export railway in its path. In the end, it was ground bearing capacity, not top speed, that shaped how Mammoet moved the dragline across Peak Downs.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Applied, invested, still outside: Pakistan is still waiting at the Brics door
articles.summary: Pakistan News: Pakistan’s attempt to join Brics remains unresolved as leaders of the grouping gather in New Delhi for the 18th summit. Islamabad formally applied for.
articles.body: Pakistan’s attempt to join Brics remains unresolved as leaders of the grouping gather in New Delhi for the 18th summit. Islamabad formally applied for membership in 2023, but India’s opposition has kept it outside the bloc.Brics originally comprised Brazil, Russia, India, China and South Africa. The grouping expanded in 2024 with the inclusion of Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran and the United Arab Emirates, becoming known as Brics+. Saudi Arabia and Argentina were also invited during the expansion process, although Argentina later declined to join.Islamabad confirmed its application in 2023Pakistan publicly confirmed its Brics membership application in 2023, when the grouping was preparing for a major expansion under Russia’s presidency.Foreign Office spokesperson Mumtaz Zahra Baloch announced the move during her weekly press briefing."Yes, I can confirm that Pakistan has made a formal request to join Brics, which we believe is an important grouping of developing countries," Baloch said.She said Pakistan had friendly relations with most Brics members and the countries invited to join the bloc. Baloch also highlighted Islamabad’s support for multilateralism and its participation in international organisations working for global peace and development."We believe that by joining Brics, Pakistan can play an important role in furthering international cooperation and revitalising inclusive multilateralism.Baloch’s statement came as the grouping prepared to admit Argentina, Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran, Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates. The new members were expected to formally join during the 2024 summit in Russia.Pakistan seeks economic support through BricsPakistan is among 29 countries that have applied to join Brics. Its bid is largely linked to its economic difficulties and the need to find new sources of funding.According to the Pakistan Economic Survey, the country’s GDP growth stood at 3.70 per cent. A report by Nikkei Asia said Pakistan had purchased a $580 million stake in the Brics-backed New Development Bank. The move was aimed at widening Islamabad’s financing options and reducing its dependence on the World Bank and the International Monetary Fund.India’s opposition keeps Pakistan outsideDespite its application and the bloc’s expansion, Pakistan has not secured membership. New Delhi’s veto power within Brics has effectively blocked Islamabad’s entry.Pakistan’s bid also comes against the backdrop of wider regional tensions and its strained relations with India. While Islamabad has sought to present membership as part of its economic and diplomatic strategy, India’s opposition remains the main obstacle.During the 2023 briefing, Baloch also called for action by Afghan authorities against terrorist groups operating from Afghanistan. She reiterated Pakistan’s support for an international peace conference on the Palestinian issue and the implementation of United Nations resolutions supporting a two-state solution.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.body: Chinese President Xi Jinping arrived in New Delhi on Saturday for the 18th BRICS Summit, beginning a two-day visit to India that marks his first trip to the country in seven years.Xi was received at the Delhi airport by Union minister of state for commerce and industry Jitin Prasada, with cultural artistes from the Northeast and other parts of India performing traditional dances to welcome the Chinese leader. We look forward to constructive discussions as BRICS continues to advance cooperation and contribute to a more balanced, representative and multipolar world.”Xi's arrival comes ahead of his bilateral meeting with Prime Minister Narendra Modi, scheduled for 6pm on Saturday.PM Modi-Xi talks amid efforts to repair tiesThe visit follows a series of high-level engagements between India and China aimed at rebuilding ties after the deadly Galwan Valley clashes in 2020 and the subsequent military standoff in eastern Ladakh.National Security Adviser Ajit Doval held Special Representative talks with Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi in Beijing last month. articles.title: Brics declaration unlikely to name any nation but condemn unilateral war imposition: Report
articles.summary: India News: NEW DELHI: Brics countries on Saturday reached an agreement on a joint declaration that is \"unlikely to name any country but will condemn unilateral w.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Brics countries on Saturday reached an agreement on a joint declaration that is "unlikely to name any country but will condemn unilateral war by any nation," Reuters reported on Saturday, citing four sources.The agreement came after intensive negotiations aimed at bridging differences among the grouping’s members, particularly Iran and the United Arab Emirates, which have taken opposing positions in the Gulf conflict.The leaders of the 11-member bloc are expected to approve the declaration later on Saturday, the sources said.The development assumes significance as the Brics summit is being held amid escalating tensions in West Asia and renewed tit-for-tat strikes between the United States and Iran. The conflict followed a pause in fighting through much of August, while Iran-aligned Houthi rebels strengthened their position in the Red Sea region.Foreign policy experts had identified the wording on the Middle East crisis as a key test for the summit. A joint statement would need to accommodate the positions of both Abu Dhabi and Tehran.Although the declaration is unlikely to immediately alter the geopolitical situation, experts said it could demonstrate unity among emerging economies and opposition to economically damaging measures such as Western sanctions.Brics foreign ministers meeting in New Delhi in May had failed to issue a joint statement because of differences between Iran and the UAE.The grouping is seeking a stronger role in shaping international rules and has called for reforms in institutions such as the World Bank, International Monetary Fund and World Trade Organization, which some members believe are dominated by Western powers.Leaders attending the summit include Russian President Vladimir Putin, Chinese President Xi Jinping, Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian, South African President Cyril Ramaphosa and Abu Dhabi Crown Prince Sheikh Khaled bin Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan.India, which maintains relations with the United States, Russia, Israel, Iran and the Gulf Arab states, is also seeking to deepen trade cooperation, reduce barriers and expand business opportunities among BRICS members.The Brics grouping comprises Brazil, China, Egypt, Ethiopia, India, Indonesia, Iran, Russia, Saudi Arabia, South Africa and the United Arab Emirates. Its partner countries include Belarus, Bolivia, Cuba, Kazakhstan, Malaysia, Nigeria, Thailand, Uganda, Uzbekistan and Vietnam.The bloc was established in 2009 and represents more than 40% of the world’s population and nearly a quarter of the global economy.India is hosting the 18th Brics Summit in New Delhi under the theme “Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability.”India began its fourth Brics chairship on January 1, having previously chaired the grouping in 2012, 2016 and 2021. articles.title: After Denmark dismantled the world’s first offshore wind farm in 2017, some blades were cut up and reused in roadside noise barriers
articles.summary: Rest of World News: Discover how Denmark repurposed dismantled offshore wind farm blades into eco-friendly noise barriers, highlighting the urgent need for sustainable solutions to impending wind turbine blade waste.
articles.body: Initially, when wind turbines were built offshore, there was no strategy for disposing of them at the end of their useful life. The solution to this issue came up in 2017, when the country shut down its first offshore wind farm named Vindeby, which had been operational in the Langelandsbælt, one of the Danish straits linking the Baltic Sea to the Kattegat, near Lolland Island, for about 26 years.Vindeby's 11 turbines were decommissioned between March and September 2017The Vindeby plant began operation in 1991 off the coast of the island of Lolland. This project featured 11 turbines, each having a power of 450 kW and manufactured by Bonus Energy, which later became Siemens. Vindeby was managed by Elkraft and later by Dong Energy, which became Ørsted. By February 2017, after nearly 26 years in service, the wind farm had reached the end of its lifespan. According to Ørsted, decommissioning began that March and was completed by September, marking the retirement of the world's first offshore wind farm. Utilizing a jack-up vessel along with a mobile crane, the blades, nacelles and towers were disassembled individually, while the concrete foundations were demolished using hydraulic shears. All equipment, including cables, was brought to Nyborg Harbour for further recycling rather than direct disposal into a landfill.Miljøskærm turned shredded blades into noise barriers near AalborgOf the 33 blades stripped from the turbines at Vindeby, some have been provided for research on how decades of seawater exposure and mechanical loads have affected the composite materials of the blades, while other blades have been assigned to the novel noise barrier technology project. A second batch of blades was used in the construction of noise barrier structures; in Denmark, Miljøskærm, a company recycling turbine blades into noise-reducing materials for road barriers, has been working on such projects ever since founder Jakob W. Nielsen first encountered the blade-disposal problem in 2011, as he told State of Green in a 2017 interview.Miljøskærm describes its process as simple. The blades are reduced to granules of fibreglass that are good absorbers of road noise due to their high density. Noise barriers using the granules were constructed on the roadside, while some of the blades were returned to the supplier, LM Wind Power, for analysis.Global blade waste is projected to reach 43 million tonnes by 2050The tale of Vindeby is a neat one, but the magnitude of what is approaching is not. Fibreglass turbine blades are difficult to recycle because they are designed to withstand decades of bending and harsh weather. Pu Liu and Claire Barlow, researchers at the University of Cambridge’s Institute for Manufacturing, presented these projections in their 2017 paper, “Wind Turbine Blade Waste in 2050”, published in Waste Management. They estimated that annual blade waste could reach 2.9 million tonnes by 2050, amounting to a cumulative total of close to 43 million tonnes. In their estimation, out of the total 43 million tonnes of blade waste accumulated by 2050, China will be responsible for 40%, Europe 25%, the US 19%, while the rest of the world will constitute 16%. This is precisely why a small experiment from Denmark counts. If only a portion of these blades can be reused as noise barriers, insulation or research material, the pressure on the 43 million-ton projection will be reduced significantly.Reuse can cut a blade's environmental impact by up to 44 percentHowever, in a follow-up study conducted after two years, the same group of researchers from Cambridge has considered the fate of a blade after it stopped rotating in a paper titled "Wind turbine blade end-of-life options: An eco-audit comparison," which was published in the Journal of Cleaner Production. They concluded that reusing a blade could reduce its overall environmental footprint by 14% to 44% compared with landfill disposal. These figures align with Vindeby's example: retired blades can be reused as noise barriers or studied for what they reveal about material durability. As more wind farms from the 1990s and 2000s reach the end of their lives, the question will be how quickly others can catch up with this small Danish company.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: A Union soldier aged just 16 to 19 was buried after the 1862 Battle of Manassas; 162 years later archaeologists found him beside four amputated limbs, and he is now set to be buried at Arlington
articles.summary: US News: More than 160 years after the Second Battle of Manassas, the remains of a young Union soldier are set to receive a final resting place at Arlington Na.
articles.body: More than 160 years after the Second Battle of Manassas, the remains of a young Union soldier are set to receive a final resting place at Arlington National Cemetery. According to the National Park Service, archaeologists uncovered the nearly complete burial of the soldier during excavations at Manassas National Battlefield Park in March 2024. Analysis indicates that he was between 16 and 19 years old and likely fought in the August 1862 battle. The excavation also recovered four surgically amputated limbs belonging to wounded soldiers who had been treated at a nearby Civil War field hospital, offering a rare glimpse into battlefield medicine and the human cost of the conflict.A burial lost for more than 160 yearsThe young soldier was discovered at a site associated with a Civil War field hospital at Manassas National Battlefield Park in Virginia. Archaeologists were conducting professional excavations in March 2024 when they uncovered his nearly complete burial. The location was connected to the Second Battle of Manassas, also known as the Second Battle of Bull Run, fought in August 1862. The battle was a major Confederate victory and resulted in thousands of soldiers being killed, wounded or captured. The soldier's remains were found along with a historic rubber pocket comb, providing a small personal detail about a young man whose name and identity remain unknown. Archaeological and forensic analysis estimated his age at approximately 16 to 19 years and indicated that he likely fought in the battle.Four amputated limbs reveal the work of battlefield surgeonsThe discovery became even more significant because archaeologists also recovered four surgically amputated limbs during the excavation. The limbs belonged to wounded soldiers who had been treated at the field hospital during the battle and were separate from the young Union soldier's burial. The discovery adds to earlier archaeological evidence from the same area. In 2014, bone fragments were uncovered during a utility project at the park. Further investigation led archaeologists and Smithsonian forensic anthropologists to a Civil War surgeon's burial pit, where they eventually identified the remains of two Union soldiers and 11 amputated limbs.The pit provided evidence of the brutal medical conditions faced by Civil War surgeons. Severely wounded soldiers were brought to temporary field hospitals, where surgeons sometimes performed amputations in an attempt to save their lives. Limbs removed during these operations could then be buried separately. The newly discovered soldier's burial is therefore significant not only because of his age, but also because of its connection to a site that preserves evidence of how wounded soldiers were treated during the conflict.What archaeologists learned from the remainsThe soldier was identified as a Union serviceman through archaeological analysis. Earlier research at the site used artefacts, skeletal evidence and chemical analysis of bones to establish that the soldiers buried there were associated with the Union Army. The 2024 excavation also showed that the newly discovered burial was separate from the earlier remains examined at the surgeon's pit. According to the National Park Service, the soldier was found with a historic rubber pocket comb, while the excavation also recovered four additional surgically amputated limbs belonging to wounded soldiers treated at the field hospital.His remains were carefully documented as part of the archaeological study. The process is being conducted under the National Historic Preservation Act, which requires appropriate consideration and documentation of archaeological resources before the remains can be transferred for burial.From an unknown battlefield grave to ArlingtonOn August 13, 2026, the National Park Service announced plans to transfer the soldier's remains to the Office of Army Cemeteries after the archaeological study and documentation are completed. The Army will then oversee his planned interment at Arlington National Cemetery. The planned burial will give the unidentified soldier a permanent resting place more than 160 years after the battle in which he likely served. It also reflects the continuing effort to identify, study and respectfully care for military remains discovered at historic battlefields.The soldier's name may never be known, but the archaeological evidence has preserved part of his story. His estimated age, connection to the Second Battle of Manassas and burial alongside evidence of battlefield surgery provide a glimpse into the experiences of young soldiers caught in one of the Civil War's major battles. The discovery also demonstrates how archaeological work can recover stories that disappeared from written history. More than a century and a half after the fighting ended, the remains of one young Union soldier are now on a path from an unknown battlefield grave to an honoured final resting place at Arlington National Cemetery.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.summary: Europe News: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has said he would travel to Miami if Russian President Vladimir Putin attends the G20 leaders’ summit schedule.
articles.body: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has said he would travel to Miami if Russian President Vladimir Putin attends the G20 leaders’ summit scheduled for December, raising the possibility of their first face-to-face meeting since Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine.Asked by DW correspondent Misha Komadovsky on Friday whether he would go to Miami for the summit if Putin were present, Zelenskyy replied, "Yes, of course. We have to come. We have to meet, to speak and make decisions," he said.Zelenskyy said the outcome of any meeting would matter more than the words exchanged between the two leaders."It's not about words. What I will tell him or what he wants to tell me, it doesn’t matter. It doesn’t matter. [...] Results matter. That's it."The Kremlin has not confirmed whether Putin will attend the Miami summit. The Russian president has not personally attended a G20 leaders’ summit since 2019.Zelenskyy highlights Canada partnershipZelenskyy made the comments while discussing agreements signed with Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney on Thursday, including a 100-year partnership declaration.He said the agreement covered several areas, including security, financing, energy, veteran policy, culture and humanitarian cooperation."So it's a global decision, a really historic decision, and I'm happy that we have it," he said.The two leaders also signed an agreement on cooperation in drone production involving several Ukrainian companies.Putin warns against Western troops in UkrainePutin’s possible attendance at the G20 summit comes as he warns European countries against sending troops to Ukraine.Speaking to reporters in New Delhi on the sidelines of the 2026 Brics summit, Putin said Russia did not threaten European countries and had no reason to seek a conflict with them."There is no such threat, and there has never been. We are not threatening European countries, nor are we going to threaten them. Why would we? No one seems to even consider that we have no grounds for any conflict with Europe. All issues were settled as a result of the Second World War. And what happened later, after the collapse of the Soviet Union, was done with the consent of the Russian Federation as the successor of the Soviet Union. Everything that runs counter to those arrangements runs counter to our interests and does not comply with the fundamental principles of international law and the UN Charter."He added, “Now they are talking about how they are thinking about bringing troops to the territory of Ukraine. This means war with Russia,” the Russian President added.Zelenskyy and Putin have not met in person since February 2022. The war has entered its fifth year, with European countries continuing to support Ukraine and the United States seeking to mediate between Kyiv and Moscow.Earlier this month, US Special Envoy Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, son-in-law of US President Donald Trump, met Zelenskyy after travelling to Moscow. Russia’s Finance Minister Anton Siluanov was also invited by the US to attend a G20 meeting in North Carolina last month, a move that angered some European officials.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: China’s Air Force One: Inside Xi Jinping’s Boeing 747-8 Presidential Jet
articles.summary: International News: While much of the world is familiar with America's Air Force One, China's presidential transport arrangements remain far less known, even though they .
articles.body: While much of the world is familiar with America's Air Force One, China's presidential transport arrangements remain far less known, even though they are based on the same variant of the iconic Boeing-747. Air travel for China's top leadership—the CCP General Secretary, President, Premier and other senior officials —is managed by the 34th Division of the People's Liberation Army Air Force, which operates a fleet including six Boeing 737-300s, two 737-700s, four 737-800s, three Airbus A319s and ten Bombardier Challenger 800s. Notably, Chinese regulations restrict the use of dedicated presidential aircraft strictly to the President and the State Council Premier for international visits, other state leaders are required to use chartered planes instead.For Xi Jinping's own long-haul international travel, the aircraft of choice has been a specially converted Boeing 747-8I, carrying Air China branding and registration B-2479, converted and tested around 2016-2017 for exclusive head-of-state use. While no official photographs have ever been released, the aircraft is widely believed to be fitted with conference tables, private bedrooms and office suites—features expected of any long-range VIP transport. In the past, China has also used converted commercial Air China Boeing 747-400 aircraft for international travel when required, with three such aircraft carrying the registrations B-2445, B-2447 and B-2472.The Boeing 747-8, the aircraft at the heart of this fleet, is the final and largest member of the 747 family ever built, stretched to 250 feet in length, making it the longest airliner in commercial service. It features a deeper, thicker wing for greater fuel capacity, larger raked wingtips for improved aerodynamics, and more efficient GENx engines borrowed from the 787 Dreamliner, pushing its maximum takeoff weight to nearly 975,000 pounds, the heaviest of any Boeing airliner.China isn't the only nation to have turned to this aircraft for head-of-state duties. VIP-configured 747-8Is have also gone to Qatar, Kuwait, Oman, Brunei, Morocco, Turkey and Saudi Arabia, the last of which is used by Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman. Interestingly, the United States itself has recently adopted a version of the same aircraft, designated the VC-25B Bridge, a stopgap presidential transport built from a former Qatari VIP jet gifted to Washington in 2025, now used by President Trump while the definitive VC-25A replacements remain under development.India, Japan, Israel, Indonesia, Singapore, Bangladesh, South Africa and a few other nations use variants of the more modern Boeing-777. The Indian Air Force acquired the Boeing-777 from Air India when the government divested from the firm. The IAF also acquired six A-321 aircraft from Air India, these aircraft will be converted to Airborne Early Warning and Control aircraft.

articles.title: San Francisco minted just 24 of these dimes in 1894 and only 9 are known to survive; 132 years later, one 10-cent coin has sold at auction for $1.25 million
articles.summary: US News: A 10-cent coin minted in San Francisco more than a century ago has just sold for about $1.25 million, turning one of the smallest denominations in US .
articles.body: A 10-cent coin minted in San Francisco more than a century ago has just sold for about $1.25 million, turning one of the smallest denominations in US currency into a million-dollar collector's prize. The 1894-S Barber dime is one of the most famous rarities in American numismatics. According to auction house Stack's Bowers Galleries, which handled the recent sale, only 24 examples were struck in 1894 and just nine are known to survive today. The coin sold for $1,250,500 at the company's 2026 auction, more than 130 years after it was made.Why were only 24 dimes made?The extraordinary story of the 1894-S Barber dime begins at the San Francisco Mint during a period of economic difficulty. The United States was still dealing with the effects of the Panic of 1893, a severe financial crisis that contributed to a sharp reduction in demand for new coinage. Against that backdrop, just 24 Barber dimes were struck at the San Francisco Mint in June 1894. They were not ordinary coins produced in large quantities for everyday circulation. The tiny mintage eventually turned the dime into one of the great rarities of American coin collecting. The exact reason for the unusual production has never been established with complete certainty. According to evidence from the San Francisco Mint, a small quantity of subsidiary coin bullion remained after recoinage and was enough to produce 24 dimes. Another long-standing story says Mint Superintendent John Daggett had the coins struck for prominent banker friends and gave some to his daughter.The competing explanations are part of what has made the 1894-S dime so fascinating to collectors. Its rarity is certain; the circumstances surrounding its creation remain partly mysterious.A tiny coin with a famous designThe coin belongs to the Barber dime series, which was designed by Charles E. Barber, then chief engraver of the US Mint. The series was produced from 1892 to 1916. The obverse features Liberty wearing a cap, while the reverse carries the denomination "ONE DIME" inside a wreath. The small "S" mint mark on the reverse identifies the coin as having been produced at the San Francisco Mint.Although collectors can find Barber dimes from other years, the 1894-S issue is in a completely different category because of its extremely small mintage and tiny surviving population. Only nine examples are currently known to exist. That means every time one of these coins comes onto the market, collectors are competing for an object that almost never becomes available.From a 10-cent coin to a $1.25 million treasureThe latest sale demonstrates just how dramatically rarity can transform the value of an old coin. The 1894-S Barber dime that recently went under the hammer sold for $1,250,500 at Stack's Bowers Galleries on September 1, 2026. The latest sale is also part of a much longer history of extraordinary prices for the coin. One of the surviving dimes has changed hands for millions of dollars in previous years, with its value driven not simply by its age but by the combination of scarcity, historical mystery and collector demand.The 1894-S dime is particularly notable because its entire known population is small enough to make each specimen significant. A coin does not need to be thousands of years old to become extraordinarily valuable; in this case, a piece of American currency from the late 19th century has acquired a status approaching that of a national numismatic treasure.The dime that helped make Dave Bowers famousThe 1894-S dime also has an important connection to Dave Bowers, the legendary American numismatist and co-founder of Stack's Bowers Galleries. According to the auction house's history of the coin, Bowers purchased an 1894-S dime in 1957, when he was just 19 years old, for $4,750. At the time, spending thousands of dollars on a 10-cent coin was an extraordinary decision for a young collector.Bowers later sold the coin for $6,000. That early transaction became an important episode in his career and helped establish his reputation in the world of rare coins. The dime therefore became connected not only with American numismatic history but also with one of the most influential figures in the modern coin-collecting business.Why this dime remains legendaryThe appeal of the 1894-S Barber dime goes beyond its face value or even its silver content. Its story combines a mysterious origin, an exceptionally small mintage, a handful of surviving examples and decades of fascination among collectors. Of the original 24 coins, only nine are known today. That scarcity means that each surviving example represents a tiny piece of a production run that was never repeated.More than 130 years after the San Francisco Mint produced those 24 dimes, one of them has once again demonstrated why the coin is considered legendary. What began as a 10-cent piece in 1894 has become an object capable of commanding around $1.25 million at auction, showing how rarity and history can turn an ordinary denomination into one of the most coveted coins in American collecting.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: 'Global South must be rule-shaper, India ready to take lead': PM Modi at Brics Summit
articles.summary: India News: NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Saturday officially declared the Brics Summit 2026 open, welcoming world leaders, including Russian Preside.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Saturday officially declared the Brics Summit 2026 open, welcoming world leaders, including Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping, to India for the two-day summit.Addressing the leaders at the opening session, PM Modi said India’s Brics chairship had followed a “people-centric and humanity-first approach”, with resilience, innovation, cooperation and sustainability identified as key priorities.Here are the top quotes:This year’s Brics Summit marks a historic milestone as we celebrate the 20th anniversary of Brics. In human life, the age of 20 marks the beginning of a new phase of maturity and responsibility. It is a stage when responsibilities are added to dreams and capabilities are given a new direction.India’s Brics chairship is based on a people-centric and humanity-first approach. Resilience, innovation, cooperation and sustainability have been our priorities. With these priorities, we have placed special emphasis on connecting the BRICS chairship with the common people. With this vision, more than 350 meetings were organised, and we had the opportunity to welcome your teams in nearly 30 cities.Today, Brics, too, is at its coming-of-age moment. Over the past 20 years, Brics has established a distinct identity on the global stage. We respect each other’s perspectives and move forward through consensus. We are not against anyone; rather, we seek to move forward with the approach of taking everyone along.Reform in UNSC cannot be delayed anymore.Global South must become a rule-shaper. The current structure of global governance appears like a pyramid. At the top, power and decision-making are concentrated, while at the bottom are countries that are affected by these decisions but have little role in shaping them. The Global South is today on the frontlines of global crises, but in the back row when it comes to decision-making. I propose a Brics continuity and implementation mechanism. Under this, all initiatives and outcomes can be followed up through the Troika. We can create a secure digital repository where, along with every decision, the nodal point, timeline and implementation status can be recorded. Friends, while strengthening Brics, we must also chart the course for global reform.For the next 20 years, we need to work on a new and ambitious agenda. We must begin this with our own working system. The Brics chairmanship changes every year, but this should not cause our institutional momentum to slow down.Friends, the message from this Brics Summit being hosted by India should be clear. If our future is shared, the right to shape that future should also be shared. From voice to impact, from privilege to partnership, this should be the guiding resolve of Brics at present.Meanwhile, in a major diplomatic breakthrough, Brics nations have reached a consensus on a Joint Statement following intensive negotiations that continued until 4 am on Saturday. The statement is expected to be issued during the summit later today.The negotiations involved differences over several contentious issues, with India leading sustained consultations to bridge competing positions and build consensus among member countries.Get the latest India News and Live updates.
